items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Well, we had a little scrap of band. ... Who was in the band? Alcee, T-Ball, myself, George, no that George, Albert Fernandez.

ctx.x: Well, we had a little scrap of band. Didn't have no name. Four, five pieces. Who was in it? Who was in it? Who was in the band? Alcee, T-Ball, myself, George, no that George, Albert Fernandez. You know him, Alcee? What did he play?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: me and T-Ball was the darkest man in the band

ctx.x: Ask him when you worked at the Absinthe House.

When did you work at the Absinthe House? It was six. That's when I went to Emris Wright. That's when I told you that me and T-Ball was the darkest man in the band. And the purist man hired his one. They don't make no price with you. They take up collections. If you make a price with them, they give you what the price is. But if you come on just for the kid, sometimes they make $20, $25, $30 a man. But if you tell him $10 a man, they give you $10. Then they come and show you they have about $160 over. And so see…
Yeah. He sang all that and that.
